absent: Definitions and widths of uevent sequence counter, buffer limit, helper path length, and netlink group numbers beyond what fragments show.
Layouts of list_head, llist_head, llist_node, linear_range, uevent_sock, net, pernet_operations, ctl_table, and ww structures.
Lock ordering, IRQ safety, and concurrency rules for test locks and global uevent list beyond single mutex protection.
Core decimal and boolean parsers for wide integers plus helpers for case folding, digit testing, power computation, and rounding.

findings.text: Per network namespace uevent service moves from allocation through socket creation to active membership and later teardown. Creation allocates a holder of type uevent_sock and creates a kernel netlink socket for family NETLINK_KOBJECT_UEVENT with group count one and handler uevent_net_rcv and flag NL_CFG_F_NONROOT_RECV, storing the holder in the namespace object. Linking into global uevent_sock_list occurs only for the initial user namespace under uevent_sock_mutex. Teardown unlinks when linked then releases socket and holder. A pernet operations descriptor binds the transitions and an early initializer registers it.

Broadcast assigns a monotonically increasing sequence number from shared counter uevent_seqnum and formats it as tagged decimal suffix with tag SEQNUM. It rejects inputs whose payload plus suffix would exceed fixed limit UEVENT_BUFFER_SIZE and treats formatting failure as memory shortage. On success it duplicates the incoming message with extra tail room, appends the suffix including its terminator, strips the netlink header, marks origin as kernel with zero port identifier and group one, then broadcasts to group one. Buffer shortage and missing listener outcomes are normalized to success while other negative outcomes propagate.

Receive validation first requires a payload pointer from the message header and fails invalid otherwise. It then resolves the owning network namespace from the socket associated with the message and requires capability CAP_SYS_ADMIN in the owning user namespace, failing permission otherwise. Valid messages delegate to the broadcast routine with the namespace socket and the acknowledgment context. A thin dispatcher forwards inbound messages to this validator through the generic netlink receive helper.

Global uevent socket collection uevent_sock_list is protected by mutex uevent_sock_mutex during insertion in namespace initialization and removal in namespace teardown. Both list mutations occur only when the socket belongs to the initial user namespace, so other namespaces bypass locking and global membership entirely.

Namespace uevent holder carries a kernel socket pointer plus a list node for global membership. Netlink configuration for creation carries a group count plus an input callback plus a flags field requesting nonroot receive. Namespace state carries a pointer to the holder. Pernet operations descriptor carries an initialization pointer plus a teardown pointer.

Early initialization registers a kernel sysctl table under the name kernel. The table exposes a single string control for the uevent helper path, delegating parsing and formatting to the generic string handler.
Helper control uses procname hotplug with access mode 0644 and maximum length defined by UEVENT_HELPER_PATH_LEN and storage pointed at uevent_helper and handler proc_dostring.

Bounded digit scanning converts up to a supplied character limit from a start value using the supplied base. It accepts decimal digits and case insensitive alphabetic digits, stopping at the first character outside the digit set or beyond the base. Accumulation uses unchecked arithmetic until high bits indicate proximity to overflow, then switches to checked multiply and add, clamping to maximum unsigned value and setting flag KSTRTOX_OVERFLOW on failure. The return combines consumed count with the overflow indicator and the output always receives the intermediate result.

Fixed width unsigned and signed converters delegate to the corresponding 64 bit parser with the caller base, propagate any negative outcome unchanged, then verify the wide result survives narrowing to the target width. Mismatched values fail with ERANGE without touching the output, while matching values store and report success.

Scaled decimal conversion proceeds through integer digits, an optional single dot, then fractional digits limited by the requested scale, followed by truncation of surplus digits, optional newline tolerance, and strict end checking. Empty integer and fraction parts are invalid unless a digit follows. A leading plus is skipped for unsigned conversion, while signed conversion handles a leading minus by negating the unsigned magnitude with sign range checks in both directions. Overflow during digit accumulation or final rescaling by a decimal power fails with range error, and any unexpected trailing character fails invalid. A scale gap beyond the decimal capacity of 64 bits also fails range when the value is nonzero.

User memory string converters bound the copy length to one less than a stack buffer, fail with fault on copy error, terminate the buffer, then delegate to the corresponding in kernel parser with the caller base or boolean target. The boolean variant uses a four byte buffer sufficient to discriminate short literals, while the generic macro sizes its buffer from the target type width to hold sign plus binary digits plus newline plus terminator.
Generic user memory conversion generator produces one function per target type and marks each generated wrapper as exported for use outside the defining object.
Flag KSTRTOX_OVERFLOW occupies the top bit of an unsigned integer, namely one shifted left by thirty one.

Three parsing shorthands forward to the bounded scanner with progressively fewer defaults. The zero option form supplies limit INT_MAX and zero start, the one option form supplies caller length and zero start, and the two option form supplies caller length and caller start.
Header guard macro _LIB_KSTRTOX_H marks inclusion of the integer conversion header to prevent repeated processing.

Selector count for a single descriptor is zero for a null pointer and otherwise the inclusive span from field min_sel to field max_sel. Array counting sums single counts and aborts with zero if any entry yields zero. Maximum value derives from field min plus the selector span scaled by field step.

Value retrieval validates that the requested selector lies within the inclusive selector interval and fails with EINVAL otherwise, then computes the base plus the offset from the minimum selector scaled by the step. Array retrieval scans entries in order for the first interval containing the selector and delegates to single retrieval, failing with EINVAL when no entry contains it.

Downward selector search reports not found and clamps to the extremes when the value lies outside the representable interval, otherwise reports found and selects the floor division result, using the minimum selector for zero step. Upward search mirrors this with ceiling division and uses the maximum selector for zero step. Array downward search iterates all entries accumulating success and stopping at the first found indication, while array upward search returns on the first successful entry. Clamping helper selects the nearest extreme outside the interval and the floor result inside without status reporting.
Linear descriptor carries a base value in field min plus inclusive selector bounds in fields min_sel and max_sel plus a per selector increment in field step.

Insertion validator requires non null neighbors with consistent cross links and requires the new node to differ from both neighbors, returning false on any violation and true otherwise. Removal validator requires non null and non poisoned neighbors with cross links pointing back to the entry, returning false on violation and true otherwise.

Corruption reporting distinguishes null predecessor or successor, poisoned successor or predecessor indicating use after removal, mismatched neighbor links indicating concurrent modification or memory error, and self alias indicating double insertion. Each case emits a diagnostic identifying the involved pointers and causes the validator to reject the operation.

Stable sort progresses from trivial length bypass through linearization to incremental merging and final relinking. Linearization breaks circularity to form a null terminated singly linked chain. Each input element joins a pending collection of power of two sized sorted runs, merging runs selected by trailing one bits in the processed count so later merges stay bounded in size ratio. After input exhaustion all pending runs merge pairwise, then a final pass rebuilds predecessor links and restores circular doubly linked form.

Both intermediate and final merges preserve stability by preferring the first input when the comparator reports equality. Intermediate merging links only successor pointers and splices the remainder of the non exhausted input, while final merging maintains both successor and predecessor pointers and appends any remainder before closing the circle.

Lock free removal loads the head with acquire semantics, reads the successor once, then attempts an atomic compare exchange to swing the head to the successor, retrying while contention is observed. Empty head yields a null result. Conditional removal performs the same sequence but fails without retry when the observed head differs from the expected node, succeeding only when the exchange installs the successor.

Correctness depends on acquire ordering on the head load paired with the atomic update, ensuring successor reads are not reordered before head acquisition. Concurrent removals are safe through retry, but callers must handle null returns and conditional failure when the head changed.

Test aliases map IRQ_DISABLE to SOFTIRQ_DISABLE with IRQ_ENABLE to SOFTIRQ_ENABLE plus IRQ_ENTER to SOFTIRQ_ENTER plus IRQ_EXIT to SOFTIRQ_EXIT.

Spin test aliases map LOCK to L with UNLOCK to U plus INIT to SI.

Conditional helper NON_RT has two alternative definitions. One variant discards its arguments to nothing for realtime builds, while the other forwards its arguments unchanged for non realtime builds.

Early boot option parser setup_debug_locks_verbose consumes a string argument to set verbosity variable debug_locks_verbose and reports handled. Global force_read_lock_recursive provides a writable flag for forcing recursive read lock behavior in tests.

Test outcome codes define FAILURE as zero with SUCCESS as one. Lock type bits define LOCKTYPE_SPIN as one and LOCKTYPE_RWLOCK as two and LOCKTYPE_MUTEX as four and LOCKTYPE_RWSEM as eight and LOCKTYPE_WW as sixteen and LOCKTYPE_RTMUTEX as thirty two and LOCKTYPE_LL as sixty four and LOCKTYPE_SPECIAL as one hundred twenty eight.
Test fixture provides two ww acquisition contexts t and t2 plus three ww mutexes o with o2 plus o3 for deadlock avoidance scenarios.
Basic test fixture provides four spin locks lock_A through lock_D plus four reader writer locks rwlock_A through rwlock_D plus four mutexes mutex_A through mutex_D for ordering and nesting checks.

Extended test fixture provides paired spin locks for families X plus Y plus Z with matching reader writer locks and mutexes, each family contributing two instances per primitive for aliasing and deadlock tests.
Per CPU fixture provides a local lock instance local_A replicated per processor for local locking tests.
